ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is the latitude value of the subsolar point, and the vertical axis is sunrise time; four curves labeled ①②③④ are marked; the dashed line φ is located near about 18° on the horizontal axis, and the position where it intersects curve ② is at about 3 o'clock on the vertical axis. Reasoning: Reading the values from the figure, when the subsolar point is at φ north latitude, the sunrise at place 2 is about 3 o'clock. Day length = 2×(12−sunrise time)=2×(12−3)=18 hours. When the subsolar point is at φ south latitude, the day length at the same place is complementary to that when it is at φ north latitude, so day length = 24−18=6 hours. Difference in day length between the two days = 18−6=12 hours.
